drivingQuestion: What must one do, and how long must one wait, between eating meat and eating cheese?
outcomeNote: The mishna's redundancy is resolved by identifying the first tanna as R' Yosei; the wiping/rinsing baraita is read as no dispute at all; the halakha on wiping is fixed, and R' Yoḥanan's 'no waiting' is re-read as cheese-then-meat.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא? וְכִי תֵּימָא: אֲכִילָה גּוּפַהּ אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ, דְּקָאָמַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא: בְּהַעֲלָאָה קָא מִיפַּלְגִי, בַּאֲכִילָה לָא פְּלִיגִי, וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אֲכִילָה גּוּפַהּ מִקּוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּמֵחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The Gemara challenges: The opinion of «Rabbi Yosei is» identical to that of «the first tanna. And if you would say» that there «is» a difference «between them» with regard to the permissibility of «eating itself, as the first tanna says» that Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel «disagree with regard to placing» meat of birds with cheese on one table, which indicates that «with regard to eating they do not disagree, and Rabbi Yosei said» in response «to» this that they also disagree with regard to the permissibility of «eating» meat of birds in milk, and this is «itself» one «of the» disputes involving «leniencies of Beit Shammai and stringencies of Beit Hillel,» one can refute this claim.

segments.he: וְהָתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים מִקּוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּמֵחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל, וְזוֹ אַחַת מֵהֶן – עוֹף עוֹלֶה עִם הַגְּבִינָה עַל הַשּׁוּלְחָן, וְאֵינוֹ נֶאֱכָל, דִּבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי. וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: לֹא עוֹלֶה וְלֹא נֶאֱכָל!
segments.en: The refutation is as follows: «Isn’t it taught» in a baraita that «Rabbi Yosei says» that «six matters» are included «as the» disputes involving «leniencies of Beit Shammai and stringencies of Beit Hillel, and this is one of them:» The meat of «birds is placed with cheese on» one «table, but» it may «not be eaten» together with it; this is «the statement of Beit Shammai. And Beit Hillel say:» It may «neither be placed» on one table «nor be eaten» with cheese. Evidently, Rabbi Yosei agrees that even according to Beit Shammai the meat of birds may not be eaten with cheese.

segments.he: אֶלָּא, הָא קָמַשְׁמַע לַן: מַאן תַּנָּא קַמָּא? רַבִּי יוֹסֵי – כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר דָּבָר בְּשֵׁם אוֹמְרוֹ מֵבִיא גְּאוּלָּה לָעוֹלָם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וַתֹּאמֶר אֶסְתֵּר לַמֶּלֶךְ בְּשֵׁם מׇרְדֳּכָי״.
segments.en: «Rather, this» is what the mishna «teaches us: Who is the first tanna?» It is «Rabbi Yosei.» The identification is important, since «whoever reports a statement in the name of the one who said it brings redemption to the world. As it is stated» with respect to the incident of Bigthan and Teresh: «“And Esther reported it to the king in the name of Mordecai”» (Esther 2:22), and Mordecai was later rewarded for saving the king’s life, paving the way for the miraculous salvation.

segments.he: תְּנָא אַגְרָא חֲמוּהּ דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא: עוֹף וּגְבִינָה נֶאֱכָלִין בְּאַפִּיקוֹרַן. הוּא תָנֵי לַהּ, וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ: בְּלֹא נְטִילַת יָדַיִם וּבְלֹא קִינּוּחַ הַפֶּה.
segments.en: § The Gemara continues discussing the consumption of poultry cooked in milk. The Sage «Agra, the father-in-law of Rabbi Abba, taught:» The meat of «birds and cheese may be eaten freely» [«apikoren»], i.e., there is no need to be strict in this matter. The Gemara notes: «He,» Agra, «teaches it and he says it,» i.e., explains his statement: The meat of birds and cheese may be eaten «without washing» one’s «hands and without wiping the mouth» between the consumption of each.

segments.he: רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב אָשֵׁי, אַיְיתוֹ לֵיהּ גְּבִינָה – אֲכַל, אַיְיתוֹ לֵיהּ בִּשְׂרָא – אֲכַל, וְלָא מְשָׁא יְדֵיהּ. אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: וְהָא תָּאנֵי אַגְרָא חֲמוּהּ דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא: עוֹף וּגְבִינָה נֶאֱכָלִין בְּאֶפִּיקוֹרֶן, עוֹף וּגְבִינָה – אִין, בָּשָׂר וּגְבִינָה – לָא!
segments.en: The Gemara relates: «Rav Yitzḥak, son of Rav Mesharshiyya, happened» to come «to the house of Rav Ashi. They brought him cheese,» and «he ate» it. Next «they brought him meat,» and «he ate» it «without» first «washing his hands.» The members of Rav Ashi’s household «said to him: But didn’t Agra, the father-in-law of Rabbi Abba, teach» only that the meat of «birds and cheese may be eaten freely?» One can infer that with regard to the meat of «birds and cheese, yes,» one may eat them without washing one’s hands in between, but with regard to the «meat» of domesticated animals «and cheese, no,» one may not.

segments.he: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּלֵילְיָא, אֲבָל בִּימָמָא הָא חָזֵינָא.
segments.en: Rav Yitzḥak «said to them: This statement» of Agra applies only if one eats them «at night,» as one cannot see whether some of the food of the previous dish still remains on his hands, and he must therefore wash them. «But» if one eats «by day, I» can «see» that no food remains on his hands, and consequently there is no need to wash them.

segments.he: תַּנְיָא: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מְקַנֵּחַ, וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: מֵדִיחַ. מַאי ״מְקַנֵּחַ״ וּמַאי ״מֵדִיחַ״?
segments.en: «It is taught» in a baraita: «Beit Shammai say:» Between the consumption of meat and milk one must «wipe» out his mouth, «and Beit Hillel say» that he must «rinse» his mouth. The Gemara asks: «What» is the meaning of the word: «Wipe [mekane’aḥ], and what» is the meaning of the word: «Rinse [mediaḥ]?»

segments.he: אִילֵּימָא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מְקַנֵּחַ וְלָא בָּעֵי מֵדִיחַ, וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: מֵדִיחַ וְלָא בָּעֵי מְקַנֵּחַ. אֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: אֵין קִינּוּחַ פֶּה אֶלָּא בְּפַת, כְּמַאן? כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי!
segments.en: «If we say» that «Beit Shammai say» that one «wipes» out his mouth with solid food «and does not need» to «rinse» his mouth with water, since they maintain that wiping is more effective than rinsing, «and Beit Hillel say» that he «rinses» his mouth in water «and does not need» to «wipe» his mouth, as rinsing is more effective, one can respond: «But» as for «that which Rabbi Zeira said: Wiping of» the «mouth» can be performed «only with bread, in accordance with whose» opinion is it? It is apparently «in accordance with» the opinion of «Beit Shammai,» since Beit Hillel do not require wiping. Yet, it is unlikely that Rabbi Zeira would rule in accordance with the opinion of Beit Shammai rather than Beit Hillel.

segments.he: אֶלָּא, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מְקַנֵּחַ וְלָא בָּעֵי מֵדִיחַ, וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אַף מֵדִיחַ. הָוֵי לֵיהּ מִקּוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּמֵחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל, וְלִתְנְיַיהּ גַּבֵּי קוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וְחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל!
segments.en: «Rather,» one must explain the dispute as follows: «Beit Shammai say» that one «wipes» his mouth after eating meat «and does not need» to «rinse» his mouth as well, «and Beit Hillel say» that in addition to wiping one must «also rinse.» This interpretation is difficult as well, since if so, this «constitutes» one «of the» disputes between them that involve «leniencies of Beit Shammai and stringencies of Beit Hillel, and» consequently, «let» the tanna of tractate Eduyyot «teach it alongside» the other disputes listed there that involve «leniencies of Beit Shammai and stringencies of Beit Hillel.»

segments.he: אֶלָּא, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מְקַנֵּחַ, וְהוּא הַדִּין לְמֵדִיחַ, וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: מֵדִיחַ, וְהוּא הַדִּין לִמְקַנֵּחַ. מָר אָמַר חֲדָא, וּמָר אָמַר חֲדָא, וְלָא פְּלִיגִי.
segments.en: «Rather,» one must interpret their statements as follows: «Beit Shammai say» that one «wipes» his mouth after eating meat, «and the same is true of rinsing,» i.e., one must rinse his mouth as well. «And Beit Hillel say» that one «rinses» his mouth, «and the same is true of wiping.» And «one Sage said one» statement «and one Sage said another» statement, «and they do not disagree.»

segments.he: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: אֵין קִינּוּחַ הַפֶּה אֶלָּא בְּפַת. וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי בִּדְחִיטֵּי, אֲבָל בְּדִשְׂעָרֵי – לָא.
segments.en: § After citing Rabbi Zeira’s statement tangentially, the Gemara discusses «the» matter «itself. Rabbi Zeira says: Wiping of the mouth» can be performed «only with bread.» The Gemara explains: «And this statement» applies only «to» bread prepared «from wheat» flour. «But with regard to» bread prepared «from barley» flour, one may «not» use it for wiping, as barley bread crumbles in the mouth and does not wipe thoroughly.

segments.he: וּדְחִיטֵּי נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן, אֶלָּא בִּקְרִירָא, אֲבָל בְּחַמִּימָא – מִשְׁטָר שָׁטְרִי. וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּרַכִּיכָא, אֲבָל בְּאַקּוֹשָׁא – לָא. וְהִלְכְתָא בְּכֹל מִילֵּי הָוֵי קִינּוּחַ, לְבַר מִקִּמְחָא, תַּמְרֵי וְיַרְקָא.
segments.en: The Gemara adds: «And even» in the case of bread prepared «from wheat» flour, «we said» the halakha «only with regard to cold» bread, «but» as «for warm» bread, it is ineffective for wiping even if made of wheat, as it softens and «sticks» to the palate, and it does not wipe the mouth properly. «And» furthermore, even if the bread is cold, «this statement» applies only «with regard to soft» bread, «but» one may «not» wipe «with hard» bread, as it also does not clean effectively. The Gemara concludes: «And the halakha is» that the use «of all items constitutes» effective «wiping, except for flour, dates, and vegetables.»

segments.he: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַסִּי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כַּמָּה יִשְׁהֶה בֵּין בָּשָׂר לִגְבִינָה? אָמַר לוֹ: וְלֹא כְּלוּם. אִינִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אָכַל בָּשָׂר – אָסוּר לֶאֱכוֹל גְּבִינָה, גְּבִינָה – מוּתָּר לֶאֱכוֹל בָּשָׂר! אֶלָּא כַּמָּה יִשְׁהֶה בֵּין גְּבִינָה לְבָשָׂר? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְלֹא כְּלוּם.
segments.en: § «Rav Asi posed a dilemma to Rabbi Yoḥanan: How much» time «should one wait between» eating «meat and» eating «cheese?» Rabbi Yoḥanan «said to him: No» time «at all.» The Gemara asks: «Is that so? But doesn’t Rav Ḥisda say:» If one «ate meat,» it is «prohibited» for him «to eat cheese» immediately, but if he ate «cheese» it is «permitted» for him «to eat meat» without delay? «Rather,» Rav Asi actually asked Rabbi Yoḥanan the following question: «How much» time «should one wait between» eating «cheese and» eating «meat?» In response to this question, Rabbi Yoḥanan «said to him: No» time «at all.»

segments.he: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אָכַל בָּשָׂר – אָסוּר לֶאֱכוֹל גְּבִינָה, גְּבִינָה – מוּתָּר לֶאֱכוֹל בָּשָׂר. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יוֹסֵף לְרַב חִסְדָּא: בָּשָׂר שֶׁבֵּין הַשִּׁינַּיִם מַהוּ?
segments.en: After tangentially citing a statement of Rav Ḥisda, the Gemara discusses «the» matter «itself. Rav Ḥisda says:» If one «ate meat,» it is «prohibited» for him «to eat cheese» immediately, as the meat contains fatty substances that stick to one’s mouth and preserve the flavor of meat. But if he ate «cheese» it is «permitted» for him «to eat meat» without delay. «Rav Aḥa bar Yosef said to Rav Ḥisda:» In the case of «meat that is between the teeth, what is» the halakha? Are these remnants considered meat to the extent that one may not eat cheese as long as they are in his mouth?

In response, Rav Ḥisda «read about him» the following verse: «“While the meat was yet between their teeth”» (Numbers 11:33). This verse indicates that even when the meat is between one’s teeth it is still considered meat, and therefore one may not partake of cheese until that meat has been removed.

segments.he: אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא: אֲנָא, לְהָא מִלְּתָא, חַלָּא בַּר חַמְרָא לְגַבֵּי אַבָּא, דְּאִילּוּ אַבָּא כִּי הֲוָה אָכֵיל בִּשְׂרָא הָאִידָּנָא, לָא הֲוָה אָכֵל גְּבִינָה עַד לִמְחַר עַד הַשְׁתָּא, וְאִילּוּ אֲנָא – בְּהָא סְעוֹדְתָּא הוּא דְּלָא אָכֵילְנָא, לִסְעוֹדְתָּא אַחְרִיתָא – אָכֵילְנָא.
segments.en: «Mar Ukva said: I am, with regard to this matter,» like «vinegar, son of wine, with respect to Father,» i.e., my practice is inferior to that of my father. «As Father, if he were to eat meat at this time, would not eat cheese until tomorrow at this time. But as for me,» only «at this meal,» during which I ate meat, «do I not eat» cheese; «at a different meal» on the same day «I» will «eat» cheese.

segments.he: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֲנָא, לְהָא מִלְּתָא, חַלָּא בַּר חַמְרָא לְגַבֵּי אַבָּא, דְּאִילּוּ אַבָּא הֲוָה סָיַיר נִכְסֵיהּ תְּרֵי זִמְנֵי בְּיוֹמָא, וַאֲנָא לָא סָיַירְנָא אֶלָּא חֲדָא זִימְנָא. שְׁמוּאֵל לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מַאן דְּסָיַיר נִכְסֵיהּ כֹּל יוֹמָא מַשְׁכַּח אִסְתֵּירָא.
segments.en: Similarly, «Shmuel said: I am, with regard to this» other «matter,» like «vinegar, son of wine, with respect to Father. As Father would patrol his property» to examine it «twice daily, but I patrol» it «only once» a day. The Gemara notes: In this regard «Shmuel» conforms «to his» line of «reasoning, as Shmuel said: One who patrols his property every day will find an asteira» coin.

segments.he: אַבָּיֵי הֲוָה סָיַיר נִכְסֵיהּ כֹּל יוֹמָא וְיוֹמָא. יוֹמָא חַד פְּגַע בַּאֲרִיסֵיהּ דְּדָרֵי פִּתְכָּא דְּאוּפֵי. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָנֵי לְהֵיכָא? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְבֵי מָר. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּבָר קַדְמוּךְ רַבָּנַן.
segments.en: The Gemara relates that «Abaye would patrol his property each and every day. One day he encountered his sharecropper carrying a load of wood» that the sharecropper intended to take for himself. Abaye «said to him: To where» are you taking «these» logs of wood? The sharecropper «said to him: To the Master’s house.» Abaye, who knew that the sharecropper had intended to take the wood for himself, «said to him: The Sages already preempted you» when they said that one should patrol his property regularly, and they thereby prevented you from stealing the wood.

segments.he: רַב אַסִּי הֲוָה סָיַיר נִכְסֵיהּ כֹּל יוֹמָא, אָמַר: הֵיכָא נִינְהוּ כֹּל הָנֵי אִסְתִּירֵי דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל? יוֹמָא חַד חֲזָא צִינּוֹרָא דְּבִדְקָא בְּאַרְעֵיהּ, שַׁקְלֵיהּ לִגְלִימֵיהּ, כַּרְכֵיהּ אוֹתְבֵיהּ בְּגַוַּהּ, רְמָא קָלָא, אֲתוֹ אִינָשֵׁי סַכְרוּהּ, [אֲמַר]: אַשְׁכַּחְתִּינְהוּ לְכוּלְּהוּ אִיסְתֵּרֵי דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל.
segments.en: The Gemara likewise relates that «Rav Asi would patrol his property every day. He said: Where are all these asteira» coins mentioned «by Mar Shmuel?» This patrol is not reaping me any benefit. «One day he saw» a water «channel that overflowed,» causing water to flood «onto his land. He took off his cloak, wrapped it, and placed it inside» the pipe to block the flow of water. «He» then «raised» his «voice,» and «people came» and «sealed» the hole. He said: «I have» just «found all the asteira» coins mentioned «by Mar Shmuel,» as I would have suffered a great loss had I not patrolled my fields.

moves.cueHe: רבי יוסי היינו תנא קמא?
moves.summary: the Gemara attacks the mishna: R' Yosei says nothing the first tanna had not already said
moves.about: whether R' Yosei's statement in the mishna adds anything at all beyond the first tanna's

moves.cueHe: וכי תימא: אכילה גופה איכא בינייהו
moves.summary: floats a defence: they differ over eating, not only over placing on the table
moves.about: whether the difference between the first tanna and R' Yosei is over eating poultry with cheese rather than only placing it on the table

moves.cueHe: והתניא
moves.summary: a baraita in which R' Yosei himself forbids eating knocks the floated defence down
moves.about: the baraita shows R' Yosei himself holds that even Beit Shammai forbid eating poultry with cheese, refuting the suggested distinction

moves.cueHe: אלא, הא קמשמע לן: מאן תנא קמא? רבי יוסי
moves.summary: the mishna names R' Yosei to teach that the first tanna is he
moves.about: what the mishna teaches by recording R' Yosei's name after the anonymous first tanna

moves.cueHe: שנאמר ״ותאמר אסתר למלך בשם מרדכי״
moves.summary: Esther's report in Mordecai's name proves that citing a statement by its author brings redemption
moves.about: proof that reporting a statement in its author's name brings redemption to the world

moves.cueHe: תנא אגרא חמוה דרבי אבא
moves.summary: Agra teaches that poultry and cheese may be eaten freely
moves.about: Agra taught that poultry and cheese may be eaten freely

moves.cueHe: הוא תני לה, והוא אמר לה
moves.summary: Agra explains his own baraita: no washing of hands and no wiping of the mouth
moves.about: Agra's own explanation that 'freely' means without washing the hands and without wiping the mouth

moves.cueHe: רב יצחק בריה דרב משרשיא איקלע לבי רב אשי
moves.summary: Rav Yitzḥak eats cheese then meat at Rav Ashi's house without washing
moves.about: he ate cheese and then meat without washing his hands in between

moves.cueHe: אמרי ליה: והא תאני אגרא חמוה דרבי אבא
moves.summary: the household objects from Agra: poultry yes, meat no
moves.about: whether one may pass from cheese to the meat of a domesticated animal without washing the hands

moves.cueHe: אמר להו: הני מילי בליליא
moves.summary: Agra's requirement holds at night; by day one can see one's hands
moves.about: why he needed no washing — by day one can see that nothing is left on the hands

moves.cueHe: תניא: בית שמאי אומרים: מקנח, ובית הלל אומרים: מדיח
moves.summary: a baraita records Beit Shammai on wiping and Beit Hillel on rinsing
moves.about: a baraita on wiping versus rinsing the mouth between meat and cheese

moves.cueHe: מאי ״מקנח״ ומאי ״מדיח״?
moves.summary: asks what the two terms mean
moves.about: what the baraita's terms 'wipe' and 'rinse' actually mean

moves.cueHe: אילימא בית שמאי אומרים: מקנח ולא בעי מדיח
moves.summary: floats a reading in which each school requires only its own act
moves.about: R' Zeira's ruling that wiping the mouth is done only with bread

moves.cueHe: אלא הא דאמר רבי זירא: אין קינוח פה אלא בפת, כמאן? כבית שמאי!
moves.summary: on that reading R' Zeira would be ruling like Beit Shammai, which is implausible
moves.about: whether each school requires only its own act and rejects the other's — a floated reading knocked down because R' Zeira would then follow Beit Shammai

moves.cueHe: אלא, בית שמאי אומרים: מקנח ולא בעי מדיח, ובית הלל אומרים: אף מדיח
moves.summary: a second reading: Beit Hillel require rinsing in addition to wiping
moves.about: a second reading: Beit Shammai require only wiping, Beit Hillel require rinsing in addition

moves.cueHe: ולתנייה גבי קולי בית שמאי וחומרי בית הלל!
moves.summary: then the case should have been listed among the leniencies of Beit Shammai, and it is not
moves.about: if this were the dispute it would belong to the list of leniencies of Beit Shammai and stringencies of Beit Hillel, where it is not taught

moves.cueHe: אלא, בית שמאי אומרים: מקנח, והוא הדין למדיח
moves.summary: each school named one act and meant both; there is no dispute
moves.about: the final reading: each school mentions one act and means both, so there is no dispute at all

moves.cueHe: גופא, אמר רבי זירא: אין קינוח הפה אלא בפת
moves.summary: the Gemara returns to R' Zeira's ruling in its own right
moves.about: returning to R' Zeira's ruling on wiping with bread, cited above only in passing

moves.cueHe: והני מילי בדחיטי, אבל בדשערי – לא
moves.summary: the bread must be wheat, not barley
moves.about: R' Zeira's 'bread' means wheat bread, not barley bread

moves.cueHe: ודחיטי נמי לא אמרן, אלא בקרירא
moves.summary: and cold, and soft — warm or hard bread does not wipe
moves.about: even wheat bread wipes only when it is cold and soft

moves.cueHe: והלכתא בכל מילי הוי קינוח, לבר מקמחא, תמרי וירקא
moves.summary: the settled halakha: anything wipes except flour, dates and vegetables
moves.about: the halakha is that anything but flour, dates and vegetables wipes the mouth — broader than R' Zeira's 'only with bread'

moves.cueHe: בעא מיניה רב אסי מרבי יוחנן: כמה ישהה בין בשר לגבינה?

moves.about: how long one must wait between eating meat and eating cheese

moves.cueHe: אמר לו: ולא כלום
moves.summary: no waiting at all
moves.about: no waiting time at all is required

moves.cueHe: איני? והא אמר רב חסדא
moves.summary: Rav Ḥisda forbids cheese after meat outright, so the answer cannot stand as asked
moves.about: R' Yoḥanan's 'no time at all' cannot be about passing from meat to cheese, since Rav Ḥisda forbids that outright

moves.cueHe: אלא כמה ישהה בין גבינה לבשר?
moves.summary: the dilemma is re-read as cheese-then-meat, where 'no time at all' holds
moves.about: the exchange is re-read as a question about waiting between cheese and meat, where 'no time at all' stands

moves.cueHe: גופא, אמר רב חסדא: אכל בשר – אסור לאכול גבינה
moves.summary: the Gemara returns to Rav Ḥisda's ruling in its own right
moves.about: returning to Rav Ḥisda's ruling itself, cited above only in passing

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב אחא בר יוסף לרב חסדא: בשר שבין השינים מהו?
moves.summary: asks whether meat lodged between the teeth still counts as meat
moves.about: whether meat stuck between the teeth still counts as meat for Rav Ḥisda's prohibition

moves.cueHe: קרי עליה ״הבשר עודנו בין שיניהם״
moves.summary: answers with a verse: it is still called meat
moves.about: meat between the teeth is still meat, so cheese may not be eaten until it is removed

moves.cueHe: אמר מר עוקבא: אנא, להא מלתא, חלא בר חמרא לגבי אבא
moves.summary: Mar Ukva waits until the next meal; his father waited a full day
moves.about: his father would not eat cheese until a full day after eating meat, while he waits only until the next meal

moves.cueHe: אמר שמואל: אנא, להא מלתא, חלא בר חמרא לגבי אבא
moves.summary: Shmuel uses the same formula about patrolling his property once rather than twice a day
moves.about: his father patrolled his property twice a day, while he patrols only once

moves.cueHe: שמואל לטעמיה, דאמר שמואל: מאן דסייר נכסיה כל יומא משכח אסתירא
moves.summary: his practice follows his own dictum that daily patrol finds a coin
moves.about: Shmuel's dictum that one who patrols his property daily finds an asteira coin

moves.cueHe: אביי הוה סייר נכסיה כל יומא ויומא
moves.summary: Abaye's daily patrol catches his sharecropper carrying off wood
moves.about: the Sages' rule about patrolling one's property forestalled the theft

moves.cueHe: רב אסי הוה סייר נכסיה כל יומא

moves.about: whether daily patrol really yields the asteira coins Shmuel promised
